citation: Burakgazi AZ. Efficacy of Electrical Stimulation on Nerve Fiber Growth in Small Fiber Neuropathy. J Clin Neuromuscul Dis 2020;21(4):187–194
text_quality: ok: publisher PDF with a text layer, 8 pages, complete (Table 1, Figs 1–2 legends, references). '±' extracts as '6' and minus signs in Table 1 as '2'. Page numbers here are PDF pages (PDF 1–8 = journal pages 187–194).
design: Prospective single-centre within-subject comparison, not randomised and not sham-controlled: each subject's ENS-treated leg against the contralateral untreated leg, the treated leg chosen by the subject. Skin biopsies read blind (Johns Hopkins Cutaneous Nerve Laboratory). Mixed-model regression and repeated-measures ANOVA.
population: Adults 18–70 with a diagnosis of idiopathic SFN. Excluded: cancer, heart disease, diabetes, vitamin deficiency, alcohol abuse, peripheral vascular disease, abnormal HbA1c, prior chemotherapy, electronic implants. Analysed: 8 (6 women, 2 men), mean age 52 ± 7, range 44–60; 2 had no detectable IENFD at baseline. How SFN was originally diagnosed is not stated ('previously diagnosed SFN').
n: 9 recruited, 1 removed for not following the protocol, 8 analysed; treated leg vs untreated leg in each (n=8 for IENFD; NCS n=4–6 per measure, baseline NCS done in only 2, older results used for 6).
setting: Carilion Clinic, Roanoke, Virginia, USA; recruitment January–September 2016.
intervention: Home neuromuscular electrical stimulation (AvivaStim XP, program 3: 50 Hz, 10 s contraction / 20 s rest) with 4 electrodes on the calf muscles (gastrocnemius and tibialis anterior) of one leg, 30 minutes, 3 days a week, for 60 days.
comparator: The subject's other, untreated leg (no sham stimulation).
duration: 60 days; assessments at baseline, day 30 and day 60.
outcomes: IENFD (3-mm punch biopsies 10 cm above the lateral malleolus, both legs, at each visit, PGP 9.5, blinded reading); nerve conduction (sural, superficial peroneal, tibial and peroneal motor); revised Total Neuropathy Score; symptoms by report.

key_results.quote: IENFD measurements on day 30 and day 60 did not show statistically significant changes in the treated group compared with the untreated group.
Only 1 subject showed some degree of meaningful growth in IENFD (IENFD was 9.8 fibers/mm on day 0; 13.3 fibers/mm on day 30; and 17.1 fibers/mm on day 60)
There was no IENFD detected in 2 of the subjects with no meaningful growth.
Subjects did not report any remarkable changes in their neuropathic symptoms.
Despite the success of previous animal studies, no meaningful nerve growth and regeneration in SFN was demonstrated with ENS therapy in this study.
Both male and female subjects between 18 and 70 years of age with a diagnosis of idiopathic SFN were included in this study.
ENS therapy for this study was delivered to 1 leg using an AvivaStim XP stimulator, with the contralateral leg serving as an untreated control.
Subjects selected which leg would receive the ENS at their baseline visit.
A trained and blinded technician then assessed the intraepidermal nerve fiber density (IENFD)

author_limitations.quote: This is a small study, which is its biggest limitation.
This may be attributed to the small sample size, stage of neuropathy, or the limited duration of the treatment.
Of the subjects enrolled in this study, 2 underwent NCS at the baseline visit while previous NCS findings were used for 6 subjects.

funding_conflicts: Carilion Clinic Research Acceleration Program (intramural grant); 'The author reports no conflicts of interest.' No trial registration is given. Internal inconsistencies: the abstract says 8 subjects and the methods 9; '54 biopsies (6 per patient)' (9 × 6) against '48 different measurements' in the discussion (8 × 6); the abstract's 'treated group compared with the untreated group' refers to legs within the same 8 people.

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Polydefkis M, Hauer P, Sheth S, et al. The time course of epidermal nerve fiber regeneration: studies in normal controls and people with diabetes, with and without neuropathy. Brain 2004;127:1606–1615 (ref 9)
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: Reference rate of epidermal reinnervation after capsaicin denervation in healthy people, which Burakgazi used to judge 'meaningful' growth; context for how fast IENFD can rise.

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Thakral G, Kim PJ, LaFontaine J, et al. Electrical stimulation as an adjunctive treatment of painful and sensory diabetic neuropathy. J Diabetes Sci Technol 2013;7:1202–1209 (ref 22)
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: Review of 8 electrical-stimulation studies in diabetic neuropathy (symptoms only, no structural endpoints); context for the Non-drug page's device evidence. No claim turns on it.
